body: Bethlehem Landfill Company owns and operates a municipal solid waste landfill at 2335 Applebutter Road in Lower Saucon Township, Pennsylvania. To expand it, the company asked the township to rezone 275.7 acres from Rural Agricultural to Light Industrial and to release two 1994 recorded instruments in the township's favor that would bar development on parts of the land. On August 14, 2023, a group of neighboring residents sued the township and the company, arguing the land was subject to Pennsylvania's Donated or Dedicated Property Act and could not be rezoned or released without Orphans' Court approval. On August 30, 2023, the township council voted to release the 1994 instruments in exchange for new conservation easements on about 193 acres, adopted the rezoning ordinance by a 3-2 vote, and approved an amended host community agreement. In December 2023 it conditionally approved the company's preliminary land development plan.

After the November 2023 election changed the council's makeup, the township stopped defending the neighbors' suit alongside the company. On April 15, 2024, the township solicitor filed a brief joining the neighbors' position, and two council members said at public meetings that the council had never voted on that change. On May 1, 2024, the council voted 3-2 to ratify the filing, over the company's objections that the motion was not on the agenda and that one council member should recuse herself. The company sued on May 15, 2024, alleging Sunshine Act violations, seeking a declaration that the solicitor's brief was void, seeking to bar the council member from voting on expansion matters, and asserting promissory estoppel based on the township's earlier promise to release the 1994 instruments. The township defendants argued, among other things, that the public ratification vote cured any violation.

On May 14, 2025, in an order amended the next day, the trial court dismissed the Sunshine Act and declaratory counts with prejudice as moot because the company had not appealed the ratification vote, dismissed the conflict-of-interest counts without prejudice and with leave to amend, and let the promissory estoppel count go forward against the township defendants. The company did not amend, discontinued the promissory estoppel count, and appealed.

In an opinion by Judge Anne E. Covey, for a panel that included Judge Stacy Wallace and Senior Judge Mary Hannah Leavitt, the Commonwealth Court held it lacked jurisdiction. An order sustaining preliminary objections with leave to amend is interlocutory, the court said, and the company had neither filed a praecipe asking the trial court to dismiss its complaint nor sought a determination of finality. The court also rejected the argument that the order was immediately appealable because it denied injunctive and declaratory relief, since the company could still pursue that relief on the counts it was allowed to amend. The court did not reach the merits.

timeline.label: Neighboring residents sue the township and the company over the rezoning and the 1994 instruments
Township council adopts the rezoning and authorizes release of the 1994 instruments
Township solicitor files a brief joining the neighbors' position
Council votes 3-2 to ratify the filing
Bethlehem Landfill files its Sunshine Act suit
Trial court rules on preliminary objections, allowing amendment of some counts
Commonwealth Court quashes the appeal for lack of a final order
